title: Range of a Rational Function via Inversion
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the range of the function r(x) = (x^2 - 1)/(x^2 + 1) by solving y = r(x) for x^2 and determining for which y-values a real preimage exists.

steps.title: Solve the Output Equation for x^2
steps.mathExpression: y(x^2 + 1) = x^2 - 1 \;\Rightarrow\; x^2 (y - 1) = -(1 + y) \;\Rightarrow\; x^2 = \frac{1 + y}{1 - y}
steps.explanation: Treating the equation as linear in the unknown x^2 and collecting terms isolates x^2 as a rational expression in y.
steps.why: y = 1 would force 0 = -2, so y = 1 can never occur and dividing by (1 - y) is safe for every candidate output.

steps.title: Impose the Nonnegativity of a Square
steps.explanation: A real x with x^2 equal to that fraction exists exactly when the fraction is nonnegative, turning the range question into a sign-chart problem.
steps.why: Squares of real numbers are never negative, and conversely every nonnegative number is a square of some real.

steps.title: Run the Sign Chart
steps.explanation: The numerator 1 + y vanishes at y = -1 and the denominator 1 - y at y = 1; between them both factors are positive, below -1 both are negative in the wrong combination, and above 1 the fraction is negative.
steps.why: A quotient of linear factors changes sign only at its zeros and pole, so testing the three intervals they create is exhaustive.

steps.title: Settle the Endpoint Inclusion
steps.explanation: r(0) = -1 attains the lower endpoint, while r(x) = 1 would require -1 = 1; also |r(x)| stays below 1 since x^2 - 1 < x^2 + 1 always.
steps.why: The numerator trails the denominator by the fixed gap 2, so the ratio can approach 1 as x grows but never touch it; the bracket closes at -1 and opens at 1.
